name: Southwest Loop — January
subtitle: Death Valley · Zion · Page · Monument Valley · Grand Canyon · Route 66
summary: A counterclockwise loop out of Las Vegas taking in five national parks and one Navajo tribal park. Warm start in Death Valley, a cold middle at elevation, and an easy Route 66 run home. Two versions are priced: a motorhome build and a car-plus-hotels build.
startEnd: Las Vegas, NV (Harry Reid International — LAS)

mustSee.name: Zabriskie Point
mustSee.why: Golden badlands at sunset, ten minutes from where you sleep. The best view in Death Valley for the least effort.

mustSee.name: Badwater Basin
mustSee.why: The lowest point in North America, 282 ft below sea level. Walk out onto the salt flats.

mustSee.name: Mesquite Flat Dunes
mustSee.why: Go at sunrise. Dunes the kids can run down, before the wind picks up and the light goes flat.

mustSee.name: Fire Wave
mustSee.why: Striped red and white sandstone at the end of a short flat walk. Valley of Fire in a single stop.

mustSee.name: Zion Canyon Scenic Drive
mustSee.why: In January the shuttle stops running and you drive the canyon yourself — a road closed to private cars most of the year.

mustSee.name: Horseshoe Bend
mustSee.why: $10 for the whole vehicle and a 1.5-mile walk. Does what a $580 Antelope Canyon tour does, for a sixtieth of the price.

mustSee.name: The Mittens at sunrise
mustSee.why: If you splurge once on this trip, splurge on a room that faces these.

mustSee.name: Desert View Watchtower
mustSee.why: Coming in from the east means this is your first sight of the Grand Canyon. It is the best one there is.

mustSee.name: Sunrise at Mather Point
mustSee.why: Snow on the rim over red rock, and the park as empty as it gets all year.

mustSee.name: Seligman, Route 66
mustSee.why: Where the Route 66 revival started. Milkshakes and old cars — this is the one the kids will talk about.

watchOuts.title: Book these three first, then everything else
watchOuts.text: Grand Canyon lodging or Trailer Village first, then Goulding's or The View at Monument Valley, then Watchman at Zion. Those three set the skeleton — everything else has slack.

watchOuts.title: Seven nights at or below freezing
watchOuts.text: Seven nights at or below freezing in the motorhome build — Zion, Page, Monument Valley and the Grand Canyon. Every one of those stops has a full-hookup option. Run the propane furnace, not the heat pump, which stops working around 40°F. Disconnect the city water hose at night and run off the fresh tank; the hose freezes long before the tanks.

watchOuts.title: Freeze damage is charged to you
watchOuts.text: Rental companies push freeze damage onto the renter and treat a burst pipe as negligent damage at full repair cost. Confirm in writing that the unit is not winterized, that the water system is live, and that they have noted your cold-weather destinations on the booking.

watchOuts.title: Death Valley is still closing roads
watchOuts.text: Flood damage persists. Bonnie Clare Road and Scotty's Castle are closed with no reopening date, North Highway has loose gravel and missing shoulders, southern Badwater Road has soft shoulders and unpaved sections, and Emigrant Campground is closed indefinitely. Check the park's conditions page a week before departure.

watchOuts.title: Fill up before you drive in
watchOuts.text: Fill up in Nevada, Utah and Arizona. Top off before entering Death Valley, where in-park fuel at Furnace Creek is notably expensive.

watchOuts.title: The park pass does not cover everything
watchOuts.text: The America the Beautiful pass covers Death Valley, Zion, the Grand Canyon and Glen Canyon. It does not cover Monument Valley, which is a Navajo tribal park ($8 per person), or Valley of Fire, which is a Nevada state park.

watchOuts.title: Price the unlimited-miles package
watchOuts.text: If the rental charges per mile at around $0.35, 1,655 miles adds roughly $580. Always price the unlimited-miles package as an alternative.

watchOuts.title: Day 13 is the weather buffer
watchOuts.text: Day 13 is deliberately short. If snow costs you a day earlier in the trip, absorb it there.

pros: Five national parks and a Navajo tribal park in one loop, out and back from a single airport.
January is the emptiest month of the year at the Grand Canyon, and Springdale and Page are both cheap in low season.
Short days: 118 miles a day on average, and five of the fourteen days involve no driving between towns at all.
Winter opens Zion Canyon Scenic Drive to private vehicles — the park shuttle does not run, so you drive it yourself.
The warm end of the trip comes first. Death Valley in the mid-60s while you settle in, before the cold middle.
One set of flights, one vehicle, one loop. Nothing is one-way.
cons: Seven nights at or below freezing once you climb to Zion, Page, Monument Valley and the Grand Canyon.
Snow at the Grand Canyon can cost a day. Day 13 is deliberately short to absorb that.
Death Valley still has flood damage: Scotty's Castle and Bonnie Clare Road are closed indefinitely, and several roads have soft shoulders and unpaved sections.
Day 12 is a 200-mile, 4h30 push from the Grand Canyon to Kingman. It is the longest day of the trip.
Two of the best stops are not covered by the park pass, and Monument Valley charges per person.
Bryce Canyon is skipped on purpose — it sits at 8,000 ft and is genuinely miserable in January.

notConsidered.reason: Strong park, but it sits on the opposite side of the map from Monument Valley. Cannot have both in 14 days.
The warmest and most kid-friendly stop available, but on the western route only.
No hookups, no potable water, no cell service, and the York Fire burned close to 100,000 acres in 2023 including much of the Cima Dome Joshua tree forest.
In January the lake is too cold to swim, which removes the main reason to go. London Bridge is a ten-minute stop.

notConsidered.place: Saguaro NP and Lost Dutchman SP
notConsidered.reason: Both good, but adding them means a 400-mile I-10 leg — the worst driving day in any version of this trip.
Sits at 8,000 feet. Genuinely miserable in January.
Trailer rentals do not include a tow vehicle, and the major rental companies prohibit towing outright. Turo treats towing as a prohibited use that voids damage protection.

moneySavers.detail: Lower Antelope now costs $80.50 per person plus a $15 Navajo permit — about $580 for six. Upper runs $115-140 per person. The famous light beams only appear between 11am and 1pm from March to October, so in January you would pay peak-adjacent prices for a canyon without its main feature.
A 1.5-mile round-trip walk, no tour, no permit. $10 total for the whole group.
A genuine slot canyon you walk yourself on BLM land, about 90 minutes from Page toward Kanab. The access road is dirt and turns to slop when wet.

moneySavers.item: Sleep in Beatty, not in the park
moneySavers.detail: The largest single lever in the car-and-hotels build.
Buy bedding and kitchen gear at a Las Vegas store on day one for $200-300 and leave it behind. Cheaper than per-person kit fees for six.
Covers Death Valley, Zion, Grand Canyon and Glen Canyon. It does NOT cover Monument Valley, which is a Navajo tribal park, or Valley of Fire, which is a Nevada state park.

options.name: Motorhome
options.summary: Transport and lodging in one vehicle. Cheapest by a wide margin, and you cook instead of eating out — but seven nights below freezing, and three places on this route it simply cannot go.

vehicle.detail: Cruise America C30 · sleeps 7 · 7 seatbelts · 30 ft long, 8.33 ft wide, 12.2 ft high
vehicle.notes: Book by seatbelt count, not sleeping capacity. The smaller C25 measures 24.93 ft long, 8.33 ft wide and 12.20 ft high — it clears Death Valley's 25-foot roads but is still too wide and too tall for Zion's Mount Carmel Highway.

lines.basis: Quoted: includes protection, unlimited miles, 15 generator hours. Kit fee declined.
Cooking in the RV with a few meals out
Bought in Vegas on day 1 instead of paying per-person kit fees
Days 1-4 economy car; the 30-footer is barred from Artist's Drive and Dante's View

costs.notes: Everything for six people for fourteen days, flights included. The America the Beautiful pass is already owned, so park entry is zero — but it does not cover Monument Valley or Valley of Fire.

pros: Food costs stay low because you cook
No lodging to book at six separate stops
cons: Cannot drive Zion's Mount Carmel Highway or reach the east side of the park
Cannot drive the Monument Valley loop — RVs prohibited by category
Needs a separate rental car for Artist's Drive and Dante's View
Tanks fill fast with six people; plan a dump roughly every other night

2.label: Not in the motorhome:
2.text: Artist's Drive is closed to vehicles over 25 ft. Take the separate rental car — it is in the budget for exactly this.

3.label: Not in the motorhome:
3.text: The final climb to Dante's View has the same 25 ft limit. Rental car again.

5.label: First freezing night.
5.text: Run the propane furnace, not the heat pump — heat pumps stop working around 40°F. Disconnect the city water hose at night and run off the fresh tank; the hose freezes long before the tanks do.

6.label: Not in the motorhome:
6.text: Mount Carmel Highway is closed to anything over 35 ft 9 in long, 7 ft 10 in wide or 11 ft 4 in high. Every Class C is about 8 ft wide and 12 ft tall, so a smaller one does not help — the whole east side of Zion is out, Canyon Overlook Trail and Checkerboard Mesa included. As of June 2026 the oversized-vehicle escort was scrapped entirely: no permit, no escort, no exception.

7.label: This is why it is 200 miles.
7.text: The direct route through the Zion tunnel is closed to you, so the day goes round via Hurricane, Colorado City and Kanab. The map shows the long way.

9.label: Not in the motorhome:
9.text: The Navajo Nation bars RVs from the 17-mile loop by category, not by size. What you can still do for free: the visitor center overlook and the 3.2-mile Wildcat Trail. A Navajo-guided 4x4 tour runs $70–95 each.

11.label: Coldest night of the trip.
11.text: Highs in the low 40s, lows in the high teens. Full hookups are available at Trailer Village — book it first, it sets the skeleton of the whole trip.

options.name: Car and lodging
options.tagline: More expensive, warmer, and unlocks three places the RV can't reach
options.summary: A seven-seater and a room every night. Roughly $2,500 to $4,700 more than the motorhome, almost all of it food and lodging — but no freezing nights, and it opens up three places the RV is barred from.

vehicle.detail: Chrysler Pacifica · Honda Odyssey · Chevrolet Suburban · 7 seats
vehicle.notes: A minivan is better for people, a Suburban better for luggage. Fourteen days from Las Vegas including airport concession fees.

costs.notes: Two versions of the same trip. "Best value" sleeps in Beatty rather than inside Death Valley, which alone saves close to $1,000 over three nights — the single biggest lever in the whole budget. "Best location" puts you inside the parks and at The View in Monument Valley.

pros: No freezing nights — real beds and heated rooms throughout
Unlocks Zion's Mount Carmel Highway and the east side of the park
Unlocks the Monument Valley loop drive
Unlocks Artist's Drive and Dante's View without a second rental
cons: Roughly $2,500 to $4,700 more than the motorhome
Six separate lodging bookings to manage
Luggage for six in one vehicle for two weeks is tight

2.label: Open to you:
2.text: Artist's Drive, with no second rental car needed.

3.label: Open to you:
3.text: The climb to Dante's View, 5,475 ft up over Badwater.

6.label: Open to you:
6.text: Mount Carmel Highway and the whole east side of Zion — Canyon Overlook Trail and Checkerboard Mesa. One of the three places the motorhome cannot go.

7.label: Shorter if you want it:
7.text: The 200 miles below is the motorhome routing round via Kanab. In a car you go straight through Mount Carmel Highway instead — about 120 miles, and the better drive. The map shows the direct route.

9.label: Open to you:
9.text: Drive the 17-mile Tribal Park Loop yourself — included in the tribal park entry, no guide needed.

days.headline: Below sea level by lunchtime
days.notes: Pick up the vehicle and drive straight in. Furnace Creek sits 190 feet below sea level and is the warmest place you'll sleep all trip — January highs in the mid-60s, lows around 40.

pois.name: Zabriskie Point
pois.caption: Golden badlands at sunset, ten minutes from Furnace Creek.

days.headline: The valley floor
days.notes: Badwater Basin is the lowest point in North America. Artist's Drive is a one-way loop through mineral-stained hills and is limited to vehicles under 25 feet.

pois.name: Badwater Basin
pois.caption: The lowest point in North America — 282 ft below sea level.

pois.name: Golden Canyon
pois.caption: An easy walk up a narrow canyon straight off the valley floor.

pois.name: Artist's Drive
pois.caption: A one-way loop through mineral-stained hills.

days.headline: Dunes and craters
days.notes: Ubehebe Crater is a 110-mile round trip from Furnace Creek. Dante's View sits at 5,475 feet and can be 25 degrees colder than the valley floor — it also caps at 25 feet.

pois.name: Mesquite Flat Dunes
pois.caption: Best at sunrise before the wind picks up.

pois.name: Ubehebe Crater
pois.caption: A half-mile-wide volcanic crater — but a 110-mile round trip.

pois.name: Dante's View
pois.caption: 5,475 ft up, looking straight down at Badwater. Can be 25° colder.

to.name: Valley of Fire State Park, NV

days.headline: Back through Vegas to the red rock
days.notes: Nevada's oldest state park. Bright red Aztec sandstone, petroglyphs, and short walks that suit kids. All campsites are now reservation-only.

pois.name: Valley of Fire
pois.caption: Nevada's oldest state park, and bright red the whole way through.

pois.name: Fire Wave
pois.caption: Striped Aztec sandstone, a short walk that suits kids.

pois.name: Atlatl Rock
pois.caption: Petroglyphs up a steel staircase.

days.headline: Into the canyon
days.notes: Enter Zion from the south at Springdale. In winter the park shuttle does not run, which means you can drive Zion Canyon Scenic Drive yourself — a road closed to private vehicles most of the year.

pois.name: Zion Canyon Scenic Drive
pois.caption: In winter the shuttle stops running, so you can drive it yourself.

days.headline: Full day in Zion
days.notes: Canyon floor is around 4,000 feet — low 50s days, high 20s nights. The mildest of the cold stops.

pois.name: Zion–Mount Carmel Highway
pois.caption: Switchbacks and the 1930 tunnel to the east side of the park.

days.headline: The long way round to Lake Powell
days.notes: Routed via Hurricane, Colorado City and Kanab. An RV cannot take the direct Mount Carmel Highway through the tunnel — see vehicle_restrictions.

pois.name: Wahweap Overlook
pois.caption: Lake Powell and the Glen Canyon Dam at the end of a long day.

days.headline: Horseshoe Bend, then the Navajo Nation
days.notes: Horseshoe Bend is $10 per vehicle and a 1.5-mile round-trip walk — far better value than a guided slot canyon tour.

pois.name: Horseshoe Bend
pois.caption: $10 per vehicle, a 1.5-mile round-trip walk. No tour, no permit.

pois.name: Wire Pass
pois.caption: Optional $6pp detour into a real slot canyon you walk yourself.

pois.name: Monument Valley at sunset
pois.caption: The Mittens as you arrive.

days.headline: Sunrise over the Mittens
days.notes: The 17-mile Tribal Park Loop is unpaved and closed to RVs and motorcycles by Navajo Nation rules. In a car you can drive it yourself. The Wildcat Trail is a free 3.2-mile loop around West Mitten Butte from the visitor center.

pois.name: Tribal Park Loop
pois.caption: The 17-mile unpaved loop drive. John Ford's Point is the classic stop.

pois.name: Wildcat Trail
pois.caption: A free 3.2-mile loop around West Mitten Butte. Open to everyone.

days.headline: In through the East Entrance
days.notes: Via Kayenta, Tuba City and Cameron. Coming in from the east means you pass Desert View Watchtower before reaching the village — the better approach.

pois.name: Desert View Watchtower
pois.caption: The east entrance. Your first look at the canyon, and the best one.

pois.name: Yavapai Point
pois.caption: Sunset, with a heated geology museum behind you.

days.headline: The rim
days.notes: Coldest night of the trip — highs in the low 40s, lows in the high teens. Free park shuttles run year-round. Snow on the rim over red rock, and the park at its emptiest all year.

pois.name: Mather Point
pois.caption: Sunrise spot, right by the visitor center.

pois.name: Bright Angel Trailhead
pois.caption: Go down as far as the 1.5-mile resthouse, then turn around.

days.headline: Route 66 westbound
days.notes: The Seligman-to-Kingman stretch is the longest intact original section of Route 66 left. Do not take the Oatman Highway — Sitgreaves Pass is steep with blind hairpins and most rental agreements prohibit it.

pois.name: Seligman
pois.caption: Where the Route 66 revival started. Milkshakes and old cars.

pois.name: Kingman
pois.caption: End of the longest intact original stretch of Route 66.

days.headline: Short day home
days.notes: Deliberately light. This is the weather buffer — if snow costs you a day earlier in the trip, you absorb it here.

pois.name: Hoover Dam
pois.caption: Park and walk out onto the bridge — 20 minutes, no ticket needed.

days.headline: Return and depart
days.notes: Allow half a day for the vehicle return process.
